title: hive bot install output (v1)
description: Stable contract emitted by `hive bot install --json` (and `hive bot install --force --json`). Idempotent: a no-op install against a matching unit returns ok=true with outcome=unchanged. Drift without --force returns ok=false with outcome=drifted and exit_code=64 so agents can branch `hive bot install --json || (test $? = 64 && hive bot install --force --json)`. Internal failures (systemctl reload/start/restart, launchctl load) return ok=false with outcome=failed and exit_code=70.

outcome.description: What happened on disk. `written` = no prior unit, new file created. `upgraded` = existing unit differed and --force overwrote it (backup_path is set). `unchanged` = existing unit already matches the rendered template. `unsupported` = autostart could not be enabled on this host. Two sub-cases: a platform with no native install path at all (target_path null), or a platform whose unit file was written but whose service manager is absent (e.g. Linux without systemd-user), in which case target_path points at the written unit so an operator can enable autostart later.

target_path.description: Absolute path of the platform-native unit file. Null only on a host with no native install path at all; set (even on the `unsupported` outcome) whenever a unit file was actually written.

backup_path.description: Absolute path of the timestamped backup file written before --force overwrote the unit. Null on outcomes other than `upgraded` and when the existing unit already matched.

restarted.description: True if this call ran `systemctl --user restart hive-bot` (Linux force-upgrade) or `launchctl unload && launchctl load` (macOS force-upgrade). False on first-time install (`enable --now` / `launchctl load`) and on no-op `unchanged` outcomes.

messages.description: Operator-facing notices emitted by the installer (binary-path fallback warnings, systemd-missing notes, etc.). Stable line shape but no schema enum — meant for human display, not programmatic branching.

error_kind.description: `drifted` = pre-existing unit differs from the rendered template and --force was not passed (recoverable, retry with --force). `failed` = a service-manager call (systemctl / launchctl) reported failure (investigate, see messages). `internal` = uncategorised.

exit_code.description: Process exit code the CLI will set. 64 = USAGE (drift, retryable with --force). 70 = SOFTWARE (service-manager failure). 1 = GENERIC (uncategorised).
